criteria.evidence: Diff shows `-## [Unreleased]` replaced by `+## [0.9.0] - 2026-08-28` with the Security/Added content retained beneath it.

Nearly every bullet has a period before the link, e.g. `Pulls go-billy to v6.0.0-alpha.2. ([#105](...), [#106](...))` and `...goes from 12 vulnerabilities to 0. ([#106](...))`; only the #104 Housekeeping bullet omits the period. Also #109–#111 are never cited (ref-name, materialized-limit, sanitize, TLS, provenance all attributed to #112).
#104 appears as a Housekeeping bullet `([#104](...))` and #105 is cited on the go-git Security bullet; identified from git history after the user flagged #104.
Security bullets reduced from multi-sentence paragraphs to one-to-three sentences each, e.g. the credentials-bound bullet shrank to three short sentences.
All 14 Security entries present before compression remain after it, each ending with a PR link.
go-git bump appears only in the Security bullet; Housekeeping now contains only the #104 golang.org/x bump.

judge.reason: The release heading, compression, consolidation and #104/#105 coverage are all in place, but almost every bullet terminates with a period before the PR link, violating the changelog's `text ([#N](...))` format that c2 explicitly requires. The replay also attributed several bullets to #112 and never cites #109–#111, which further undermines the link back-fill even though c3's literal scope (#104, #105) is satisfied.
